The fix is straightforward — add `.distinct()` to the final queryset so shared attributes across multiple product types aren't returned multiple times.

The change is complete. 

The bug was in `filter_attributes_by_product_types` at `saleor/graphql/attribute/filters.py:79-81`. When multiple product types in a category/collection share the same attribute, the `qs.filter(Q(product_types__in=...) | Q(product_variant_types__in=...))` produces a row per matching join, yielding duplicate attributes.

Adding `.distinct()` deduplicates the result set while keeping each shared attribute present exactly once. Since this function is the shared implementation invoked by both the legacy `filter` path and the newer `where` path, and it handles both `in_category` and `in_collection`, the fix covers all four required variants.
